facts.text: Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 was cold rolled longitudinally to 20%, 50%, or 80% thickness reduction using 0.1 mm reduction per pass and a roll linear velocity of 600 mm/s.
The 80%-cold-rolled alloy was annealed for 20 min at 650, 700, 750, or 800 °C.
Room-temperature tensile tests were performed at a crosshead speed of 1 mm/min, with three tests for each processing condition.
The alloy retained a single BCC phase after cold rolling, including at 80% thickness reduction.
Cold rolling increased the low- and medium-angle grain-boundary fraction from 53.0% in the as-cast state to 84.9% after 80% reduction.
Increasing the annealing temperature raised the recrystallized fraction from 15% at 650 °C to 49.1% at 800 °C.
Rolling-induced dislocation tangles and walls, grain-boundary changes, and strong texture impeded dislocation motion and produced work hardening.

Higher-temperature annealing promoted dislocation rearrangement and annihilation and the nucleation and growth of strain-free recrystallized grains, reducing strengthening barriers and facilitating slip.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, increasing cold-rolling reduction increased tensile strength and decreased elongation.
At 80% rolling reduction, tensile strength was 1408 MPa, about 40% above the as-cast value of 1007 MPa, while elongation decreased from 23% to 10.5%.
For the 80%-rolled alloy, increasing annealing temperature decreased tensile strength and increased plasticity relative to lower-temperature or unannealed conditions.
After 20 min annealing, tensile strength decreased from 1251 MPa at 650 °C to 1069 MPa at 800 °C, while elongation increased from 11% to 17%.
